Under exponential transport, total transmittance becomes the product of individual transmittances: $T_{\mathbf{o}, \mathbf{w}}(t) = \exp \left( - \int_0^t \sum_i \sigma_i(\mathbf{o} + s\mathbf{w}, \mathbf{w}) ds \right) = \prod_i T_{\mathbf{o}, \mathbf{w}}^{(i)}(t)$ [S1].

The claim states that under exponential transport, total transmittance is the product of individual transmittances, expressed as $T_{O, w}(t) = exp(-int_0^t sum_i sigma_i(o + sw, w) ds) = prod_i T_{O, w}^{(i)}(t)$. Source [S1] explicitly derives this relationship in equations (19), (20), and (21). Specifically, it states that statistical independence implies the total coefficient is the sum of individual coefficients ($sigma = sum sigma_i$), and under exponential transport, this leads to the total transmittance being the product of individual transmittances, matching the formula in the claim exactly.
